topic: Built-in browser reconciliation and browser-capability canon lock for Puppet Master rewrite planning docs.
objective: Replace stale browser canon with the locked PM browser model and synchronize browser UI, capture, permissions, storage, runtime artifacts, testing/tooling, and wiring docs around one coherent owner-driven contract.
decisions: The built-in browser is separate from `web_search`, `web_fetch`, and Site Reader / Reading Site. It is a real PM-controlled browser surface for direct user browsing, watchable live automation, screenshots, DevTools, auth/device flows, and deterministic capture into chat.

The canonical browser architecture is CEF-class embedded Chromium with a PM-managed pinned bundled runtime updated atomically as a matched set. Preferred integration is lower-level bindings plus a PM-owned shim/bridge. Native child-window embedding is the baseline host path; offscreen rendering is secondary.

The primary browser host is the editor/workspace tab surface. The bottom panel is not the primary browser host; it may only expose browser-adjacent logs, evidence, downloads, console/network summaries, or DevTools-adjacent panes.

HTML open semantics are `Open` for source, `Open in Browser` for `workspace_preview`, and `Open in Detached Browser` for `detached_preview`; split is a second-step layout action rather than a separate open command.

Canonical browser session classes are `workspace_preview`, `detached_preview`, `automation_session`, and `auth_session`. `workspace_preview` is project-persistent, `detached_preview` shares origin state unless explicitly separate, `automation_session` is separate and ephemeral by default, and `auth_session` is isolated for PM-owned auth flows.

Direct user interaction with an `automation_session` triggers `Take over and pause agent` (default), `Let agent continue`, or `Stop agent and keep browser`. A paused automation browser remains `automation_session`; only `Promote to Normal Browsing` reclassifies it.

Browser capture is explicit and user-triggered only. Browser element picks use `browser_element_context`, browser text selections use `browser_selection_context`, native document selections continue to use `document_selection_context`, and capture creates removable composer chips that never auto-send a hidden message. If there is no writable active composer, PM opens a new thread.

Supported browser capture labels are `Add Selection to Chat`, `Add Selection + Screenshot`, `Add Selection + Full Screenshot`, `Pick Element for Chat`, `Pick Element + Screenshot`, `Pick Element + Full Screenshot`, `Add Screenshot to Chat`, and `Add Full Screenshot to Chat`. The default combined capture is context plus clipped screenshot.

DevTools supports docked and detached modes; docked is default and there is only one focused-browser docked DevTools instance at a time. Strong named actions are the guaranteed browser contract; raw CDP or arbitrary browser-code execution is not the core guaranteed interface.

Guaranteed everyday browser actions are `navigate`, `back`, `reload`, `open_tab`, `select_tab`, `close_tab`, `click`, `type`, `fill_form`, `select_option`, `hover`, `drag`, `press_key`, `upload_file`, `handle_dialog`, `wait_for`, `verify_text`, `verify_element`, `verify_value`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `console`, `network`, and `set_viewport`. Advanced actions are `trace_start`, `trace_stop`, `video_start`, `video_stop`, `export_pdf`, `storage_import`, `storage_export`, `cookie_*`, `local_storage_*`, `session_storage_*`, `network_offline`, `network_online`, `route_mock`, and `generate_locator`.

Browser permissions use three layers: always allowed, session-granted, and high-risk explicit confirmation. Canonical browser runtime fields are `session_class`, `requested_browser_runtime`, `effective_browser_runtime`, `requested_capabilities`, `effective_capabilities`, `capability_degradations`, `blocked_actions`, `permission_tier`, `profile_scope`, `restore_policy`, and `takeover_state`. Degradation reasons are `platform_unsupported`, `runtime_unavailable`, `permission_not_granted`, `session_class_restricted`, and `temporarily_unavailable_after_recovery`.

Normal browser sessions restore; live automation and auth sessions do not silently resume active work after restart. Browser or browser-subprocess crash preserves recoverable metadata, preserves completed evidence artifacts when possible, and offers `Reopen`, `Retry`, and `Keep Closed`. Browser screenshots, traces, videos, and recordings flow through the shared runtime artifact/evidence pipeline.

Reconciliation verified `Contracts_V0.md`, `Project_Output_Artifacts.md`, `Progression_Gates.md`, `Tools.md`, and `newfeatures.md` as verification-only for this packet; no direct packetized edits are emitted for those files.

anchors.anchor: ### 9A. Browser tab and detached preview normalization (2026-03-08)
anchors.content_markdown:
The canonical browser container model is editor/workspace-tab-first for in-shell browsing.

Rules:
- in-shell normal browsing uses browser tabs in the editor/workspace surface, not a free-floating browser-instance pool
- detached preview/browser windows are first-class and outside the in-shell browser-tab cap
- bottom-panel browser hosting is not canonical behavior
- LRU browser-instance reuse is not canonical behavior
- `automation_session` and `auth_session` are not counted as normal in-shell browser tabs

Rendered selection capture uses three canonical typed attachments: `browser_element_context` for browser/HTML element capture, `browser_selection_context` for browser text selection capture, and `document_selection_context` for native document selections.

`browser_selection_context` carries bounded browser-selection provenance including `browser_session_id`, `session_class`, `page_url`, bounded `selected_text`, `selection_anchor?`, `requested_target`, `effective_target?`, `truncation_state`, and `captured_at`.

Composer behavior:
- capture creates a visible pending composer chip/card immediately visible to the user
- chips are stored in composer-prep state keyed by `thread_id`
- the chip attaches to the next submitted user message by default and may be removed before send
- capturing browser context MUST NOT silently inject a hidden message into the thread
- if the owning thread is terminal or non-writable, create a new thread in the same owning surface and record both `requested_target` and `effective_target`

anchors.anchor: ### 1.2A Structured attachment normalization for browser element context
anchors.content_markdown:
Before final conversation payload emission, the prompt pipeline MUST normalize structured user attachments created by chat/composer surfaces, browser surfaces, and native document review surfaces.

For `browser_element_context`, normalize bounded element summary fields before the user's freeform message text.

For `browser_selection_context`, serialize bounded `browser_session_id`, `session_class`, `page_url`, bounded `selected_text`, `selection_anchor?`, `requested_target`, `effective_target?`, and `truncation_state` before the user's freeform message text, and never inject unbounded DOM or page bodies.

For `document_selection_context`, keep the existing bounded native-document fields and never repurpose the type for browser text selection.

Blocked or expired chips MUST NOT be serialized as successful user attachments.

The prompt stage order remains resolve config -> resolve Persona -> resolve effective runtime -> resolve skills -> compile context -> normalize structured attachments -> assemble Instruction Bundle -> attach tool schemas -> finalize.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/FileSafe.md

Browser capability layers are runtime capability gates for agent/tool-driven browser actions.

| Browser action family | Effective layer | Default behavior | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| navigation / readback | always_allowed | allow when the browser runtime is healthy | still blocked by `runtime_unavailable` or recovery state |
| explicit share/capture actions | always_allowed | allow | capture is user-triggered and does not auto-send hidden chat messages |
| interaction, tab management, viewport, upload, dialog, trace, and video control | session_granted | ask/allow based on the resolved session permission snapshot | applies to agent/tool-driven interaction |
| auth-flow actions, storage import/export, cookie/storage mutation, offline/mock routing, download execution, and promotion into normal browsing | explicit_confirmation | deny until explicitly confirmed | treated as high-risk state mutation |

Requested versus effective browser disclosure must include runtime, capabilities, degradations, blocked actions, session class, permission tier, profile scope, restore policy, and takeover state.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/Contracts_V0.md

anchors.anchor: #### Additions: Preview session + browser rendering persistence contract
anchors.content_markdown:
Preview persistence MUST support both document-backed and artifact-backed subjects through `preview_subject_id = doc:<document_id>` or `artifact:<artifact_id>`.

Required redb keys:
- `preview_state.v1:{project_id}:{preview_subject_id}`
- `preview_source_artifact.v1:{project_id}:{artifact_id}`
- `browser_session_state.v1:{project_id}:{browser_session_id}` with `session_class`, requested/effective runtime, requested/effective capabilities, degradations, blocked actions, permission tier, profile scope, restore policy, and takeover state
- `browser_profile_state.v1:{project_id}:{profile_scope}` for persistent normal-browsing state

Partitioning rules keep `workspace_preview` project-persistent, `detached_preview` origin-linked unless explicitly separate, `automation_session` ephemeral, and `auth_session` isolated.

Required browser events are `browser.session.created`, `browser.session.state_changed`, `browser.session.takeover_state_changed`, `browser.session.promoted`, `browser.session.closed`, `browser.context_captured`, and `browser.evidence.created`.

Restore eligibility keeps normal browser sessions restorable by project/workspace identity while `automation_session` and `auth_session` do not silently resume active live work after restart.

Browser recovery rules preserve recoverable metadata and completed evidence when possible, reopen automation/auth sessions as stopped or attention-required, and use `Reopen`, `Retry`, and `Keep Closed` as the canonical recovery actions.

Promotion from paused automation into normal browsing copies/promotes eligible state into a normal browser profile and changes future restore behavior accordingly.

`PreviewSession` remains a durable runtime contract for rendered subject identity, but browser-capable surfaces layer a distinct browser-session identity on top of preview identity so that browser tabs, detached windows, automation sessions, and auth sessions do not collapse into one broad preview-instance model.

Identity rules:
- moving the same preview subject between source-linked preview surfaces keeps the same `preview_session_id` when `preview_subject_id` and `source_revision` remain unchanged
- browser-capable surfaces additionally carry a distinct `browser_session_id` and `session_class`
- detaching normal browsing is an attachment change, not a new preview subject, unless the user explicitly creates a separate detached profile
- `bottom_panel_browser` is not a canonical attachment target

anchors.anchor: #### Platform runtime matrix and degraded-mode UX
anchors.content_markdown:
The rendering system must define one browser product model across supported desktop platforms: a PM-managed pinned bundled CEF-class Chromium runtime with editor-tab primary hosting and first-class detached windows.

Required doctor/preflight checks validate bundled browser runtime health, version match, browser startup path, and both editor-tab and detached host paths under the same PM browser abstraction.

Browser runtime failure must not silently swap to an unrelated legacy webview/browser model.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md, ContractName:Plans/newtools.md, ContractName:Plans/Permissions_System.md

Browser recordings and adjacent browser evidence must preserve the canonical browser session distinction.

- evidence from `workspace_preview` or `detached_preview` retains owning project/workspace/browser-session identity
- evidence from `automation_session` or `auth_session` does not imply that the underlying browser session is a persistent shell browser tab
- screenshots, traces, videos, and recordings emitted from browser sessions route through the shared runtime artifact pipeline
- actions such as `Send to Chat`, `Open`, or `Focus Browser` route back to the owning canonical browser session rather than invent a separate artifact-owned browser shell

Browser evidence artifacts must carry enough metadata to rejoin the owning browser session and project context.

ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md, ContractName:Plans/storage-plan.md, ContractName:Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md

anchors.anchor: ### 14.1 End-to-end flow: tool selection → launch → interaction → evidence capture → chat display
anchors.content_markdown:
For browser-capable web runs, the PM built-in browser `automation_session` is the canonical visible browser target. External Playwright/CDP attach modes may exist as implementation techniques or compatibility paths, but they do not replace the built-in browser product model.

Desktop/mobile visible providers remain valid for native app and simulator/emulator targets and continue to use the shared evidence contract.

anchors.anchor: ### 14.3 Coexistence with headless mode (default/CI fallback policy)
anchors.content_markdown:
Local default remains `visual_mode = auto`, CI default remains `visual_mode = headless`, `forced_visible` fails fast if visible prerequisites are missing, and `forced_headless` skips visible launch steps.

For browser-capable web runs, the visible path is the PM built-in browser `automation_session`; missing PM browser runtime prerequisites surface as `runtime_unavailable`, and forced-visible mode must fail fast rather than silently swapping to a different browser product model.
